request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: [redacted]
Age: 12
Sex: Female
Date of Admission: [redacted]
Date of Discharge: [redacted]

Hospital Course:
The patient presented to the emergency room with intense left flank pain, which was discovered to be caused by an obstructing calculus in the left ureter and nephrolithiasis. The patient was treated with pain control medications and hydration, and subsequently referred to a nephrologist. The patient underwent a "stone risk study" and renal ultrasound, which showed multiple bilateral cysts and renal calculi. Genetic testing was performed and identified dual mutations in GANAB and PKD1genes. 
Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Discharge Instructions:
-The patient should follow up with the nephrologist for further evaluation and management of the polycystic kidney disease.
-The patient should return if she experiences any further pain or symptoms.

Follow-up:
The patient will follow up with the nephrologist for further evaluation and management of the polycystic kidney disease.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
The admission was for flank pain caused by an obstructing left ureteric calculus with nephrolithiasis. The patient was treated with analgesia and hydration. Polycystic kidney disease was identified afterward, and the follow-up is for that condition.

The principal diagnosis is the condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the admission. Here that is the obstructing ureteric calculus, which caused the pain and the ED presentation. The polycystic kidney disease (Q61) is an underlying finding, and the discharge plan is outpatient follow-up for it.

The candidate codes for the calculus are N20 (calculus of kidney and ureter) and N13 (obstructive uropathy). N20.1 is the ureter calculus code. With hydronephrosis, N13.2 would apply, but hydronephrosis isn't documented. Obstruction by a calculus without hydronephrosis codes to N20.1.

CODE: N20
